approachQuestion.prompt: Given n positive parcel weights and target T, count subsets of parcel indices totaling exactly T, modulo 1000000007. Equal weights at different indices are distinct choices. Examples: [2,2,3], T=4 → 1; [2,2,3], T=2 → 2; [5], T=0 → 1. Which approach is most suitable?
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200; 1 ≤ weights[i] ≤ 1000; 1 ≤ T ≤ 20000, with T=0 also accepted as an immediate return of 1. Input is read-only. Return only the modular count.

options.text: Initialize ways[0]=1 and other entries through T to zero. For each weight w, update s from T downward to w by adding ways[s−w] modulo the modulus.
options.feedback: A subset either omits the current parcel or includes it exactly once. Descending updates keep these categories disjoint and preserve multiplicity of equal-weight indices.

options.text: Store a row of counts for every parcel prefix and sum, adding omit and include counts from the previous row.
options.feedback: This computes the correct result on the whole domain, but retains old states that future transitions never read. Removing those states preserves correctness and reduces auxiliary storage.

options.text: Use Boolean reachability and return one when T is reachable, zero otherwise.
options.feedback: For [2,2,3], T=2 there are two subsets but a Boolean state returns one.

options.text: Deduplicate equal weights before running the descending count update.
options.feedback: For [2,2,3], T=2 this loses one of the two distinct single-parcel choices.

feedback.reason: Count distinct indexed choices rather than collapsing a counting state into reachability.
details: For positive T allocate T+1 counters, initialize ways[0]=1, and process all n weights with descending sum updates. For T=0 return one immediately.

Parcel indices are distinct choices even when weights match. Descending updates prevent using one index twice. Positive weights mean target zero has exactly the empty subset, allowing the specified immediate return.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For positive T allocate T+1 counters, initialize ways[0]=1, and process all n weights with descending sum updates. For T=0 return one immediately. Analyze this fixed implementation. Use n for parcel count and T for the positive target in the asymptotic pair; N=n. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Array indexing and word arithmetic take constant time. No hashing, amortized containers, recursion, slicing, or input copying is used. Count all allocated work arrays and temporaries; exclude the read-only input and scalar output.
Include initialization; treat the stated dimensions as variable parameters within their bounds. Use a word per stored counter or flag, not a packed bitset.

feedback.reason: For positive target, update one T+1 count array per parcel.
details: Each of n parcels can update T sums; small weights attain this worst case. The array has T+1 word counters. T=0 takes constant work. No subset lists, recursion, hashes, or copies are created.
“O(n+T) time, O(T) auxiliary space”: Each parcel may update nearly every sum. Adding n and T omits the repeated sum scan.
“O(nT) time, O(nT) auxiliary space”: The method stores one sum array, not a sum row for every parcel.
“O(nT) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Descending updates prevent reuse but still retain all T+1 counters.
